answer: The bridge multiplier is published, charged in terrace, and velvet lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2709 identities would post 4219 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
